items.title: 63476_Jimmie Crawford oral history interview
items.q: The man was a natural athlete, a good musician, and above all he was one of the greatest gentlemen that I ever met in my life. I loved the man.

ctx.x: Now, this woman was an amazing lady, without any formal education whatsoever, because she couldn't write, read nor write. My grandfather was the same a saint. They were the only parents I had besides an aunt, who's dead now, who lived across the street, and one of my grandfather's (inaudible).

Now, I started out, as I forestated, with an orchestra leader (inaudible). He was an athletic instructor there, Jimmy Lunsford. He finished Fisk University, and then he came to New York. Pardon me. He took up postgraduate work at Columbia University, and also he tried to join Fletcher Henderson's band, but he didn't make it.

So he came back to Memphis. Now, he finished Fisk University, which was in Nashville, but he came back to Memphis to accept a job there as athletic instructor. The man was a natural athlete, a good musician, and above all he was one of the greatest gentlemen that I ever met in my life. I loved the man. He's dead now, of course, and we started out from scratch.
